headline: Record quarter as revenue and profit surge, guidance raised

kpis.label: Net income attributable to common stock (GAAP)

summary_short: Quanta's second-quarter 2026 revenue rose 41.1% y/y to $9.56 billion and GAAP diluted EPS nearly doubled to $2.96, while adjusted EBITDA grew 59.5% to $1.07 billion; the company significantly raised its full-year 2026 guidance across every metric.
summary_long: Revenue rose 41.1% y/y to $9.56B and consolidated operating margin expanded to 7.3% from 5.5%, led by Electric segment growth. GAAP diluted EPS nearly doubled to $2.96; adjusted diluted EPS rose 71.0% to $4.24. Free cash flow surged to $886.0M from $170.4M a year ago. Cash was flat at $506.4M as $1.24B of acquisition spending (Phalcon, Percheron, PSD) was funded mostly by debt draws; these deals, plus July's Enerfab close, did not materially contribute to Q2 results. Total backlog hit a record $53.4B. Quanta significantly raised FY2026 guidance across every metric, citing Q2 outperformance, improved second-half visibility and expected acquisition contribution.

drivers.explanation: Electric segment revenue +43.6% y/y to $7.84B (82.0% of total, up from 80.6%); Underground and Infrastructure revenue +30.7% y/y to $1.72B (18.0% of total).
Recently acquired Phalcon, Percheron and PSD (closed in Q2) 'did not materially contribute' to Q2 results; Enerfab closed in July 2026 and will contribute from Q3.
Consolidated operating margin expanded to 7.3% from 5.5% (+180bp): Electric margin 11.5% vs 10.1% (+140bp), Underground and Infrastructure 9.1% vs 6.9% (+220bp).

drivers.metric: Net income attributable to common stock (GAAP)
drivers.explanation: Revenue growth outpaced cost growth; partly offset by higher SG&A ($698.5M vs $528.4M) and acquisition-related intangible amortization ($157.0M vs $113.2M).
Operating cash flow rose to $1,095.4M from $295.7M y/y on working-capital timing; net capex rose modestly to $209.5M from $125.3M.
Record backlog driven almost entirely by the Electric segment, whose total backlog rose to $43.79B from $30.28B y/y; not further explained in the release.

Raised on Q2 outperformance, improved second-half visibility, and expected contribution from Phalcon, Enerfab, Percheron and PSD (~$1.2-1.4B revenue, ~$120-140M adjusted EBITDA for FY2026 in aggregate).

CEO Duke Austin attributed results to the 'compounding strength and momentum' of Quanta's operating model and self-perform craft-skilled workforce; cited improved back-half visibility and recently closed acquisitions in raising full-year guidance across all metrics.
